div.head:
TO THE MOST INVINCIBLE AND MOST CHRISTIAN
KING HENRY III
OF FRANCE, AND FIRST OF POLAND

opener.salute: To the supreme favor which Your Majesty has deigned to show me

div.p: by coming to my humble dwelling and carrying away with you my portrait, in exchange for that living image of your heroic virtues and your divine worth which you have left impressed within the very center of my heart; an exchange for me both exceedingly fortunate and blessed: I am unable to respond, not even in thought or in desire.

For what could possibly come from me that might be worthy of the sublime greatness of your heavenly spirit and your blessed fortune? Nor can I, by any expression of gratitude, repay even in part the infinite merit of the gracious and generous promises you made to me concerning the book that I am preparing to dedicate to you, promises worthy of your greatness and of your most serene royal splendor far more than of any quality of my own.

Yet, just as the whole world may sometimes be depicted within the narrow space of a single sheet of paper, so in these few verses, which I reverently send to Your Majesty, I have attempted to sketch, however briefly and imperfectly, my gratitude and my boundless and most ardent desire to celebrate, beyond every limit of earthly hope, the innumerable and superhuman gifts that happily dwell within your noble breast.

closer.salute: With devout and singular affection, I humbly bow before Your Majesty and reverently embrace your sacred knees.
closer.signed: Your Majesty's most humble and most devoted servant, Veronica Franco.

lg.l: As from heaven down to a humble roof
Beneficent Jove descends to us here below,
and to avoid blinding mortal eyes
with such a noble sight, takes human shape:
so to my poor dwelling came Henri,
without royal show, which blinds and dazzles,
Henri, whom fate chose for such an empire
that one world alone cannot contain it.
Even so disguised, into my heart
he shone such a ray of his divine virtue
that my innate strength completely failed me.
So, assured of the depth of my affection,
he took my image, in enamel and paint,
away with him in a gracious, open spirit.
Take, king, sum of virtue and perfection,
what my hand reaches out to give you:
this carved and colored countenance,
in which my living, real self is represented.
And if such a lowly and imperfect image
is not what your blessed gaze expects,
consider my motive rather than the result.
A small spark can still kindle a great flame.
And because your undying, celestial valor,
tested by a thousand trials in war and peace,
filled my soul with noble wonder,
so the desire felt in a woman's heart
to raise you above heaven, beyond this world,
see, expressed and proved, in this likeness of me.
